+- `syntax.js` reaches `parser` and `printer` through getters: parsing never loads the printer, and the printer loads the parser for its `parse` phase, which reads an asset with it — building the printer's tree as each statement finishes, rather than converting a tree. `parse.webpackParser` defaults to true and turns that off; terser's own parser reads what it reads its own way (`parse.expression`, `parse.strict`, TypeScript, a line opening an HTML comment) and whatever webpack's parser refuses.

- `syntax-parser.js` — tokenizer, acorn-derived core and every production in one file (any parse reaches the productions, and the coming struct-of-arrays rewrite moves node creation through them). `regexp.js` (pattern validator) is the one on-demand piece, reached only for a pattern the host engine rejected — never `require` it from a build path.

-- `syntax-printer.js` — webpack's JavaScript minifier, terser's design ported to write byte for byte what terser writes; `jsMinify.js` (the `minify` the default minimizer dispatches JS to) goes through it when given `printer: true` — which `optimization.minimizeOptions.javascript` defaults to under `experiments.futureDefaults` — and through terser as published otherwise — the user's own, as `terser-webpack-plugin` brings it, since webpack lists terser only as a devDependency; the printer itself never loads terser. `createModules` builds what terser's modules exported — the node classes from `nodeClasses()` (`createAst`), the parser (`createTerserParser`), the compressor and the output stream — and each entry of `PHASES` installs one part onto them: add phases there and nowhere else. `correct` wraps the methods with which terser writes a wrong program and changes only that output; `corrections.enabled` switches it off. `improve` writes less where terser's longer program provably runs the same — after compressing, a statement calling a function in place with nothing passed runs its body there — and `improvements.enabled` switches it off. The `parse` phase builds the tree from `syntax-parser.js` (`createTerserTree`), leaving to the ported parser a source terser reads unlike the spec; `syntax-printer-parse.unittest.js` holds that to terser's parse over acorn's corpus, `syntax-printer-terser-parser.unittest.js` the ported parser and `syntax-printer-estree.unittest.js` the ESTree conversion. `test/specCases/minify-corpora.spectest.js` holds the whole printer to terser's output, errors included, over each corpus in its `CORPORA` list (add a new one there) under the option sets in `OPTION_SETS`, and runs each output whose test states what its input prints (terser's `expect_stdout`, swc's `expected.stdout` and `exec.rs`) in terser's sandbox. A byte difference is accepted only where switching the `correct` and `improve` phases off gives terser's bytes back, and fails where `improve` writes more than without it; what it fixes is listed in `CORRECTED` (printing right with the phase, as terser without), and an output misprinting as terser's by an option's own contract in `INHERITED`, each with the reason — an entry that stops matching fails until retired. Each output is also sized against swc's recorded one, a fixture's `output.js` or, for one of terser's cases, what swc's port of it records (gzip decides, raw breaks a tie): one bigger fails unless `test/helpers/swcSmaller.js` lists it under what swc does that webpack does not yet, and a listed one no longer bigger fails until retired. Under the default minimizer's options each source of every corpus but test262 is also minified by `oxc-minify`, held the same way to `test/helpers/oxcSmaller.js`; an oxc output that misprints is no lead. `JS_MINIFY_REPORT=<file>` tallies where webpack's is worse, the same and better. terser's corpus submodule is pinned to the `terser` devDependency — bump both together, and regenerate `data.js`.
